facts.raw_span: left testicular bloating and dull pain for 20 years
acutely worsening over the past 10 days
denied other medical history
the left testis was enlarged, firm, smooth, without discrete nodules or tenderness
transillumination was negative
bilateral epididymal cysts (largest 0.67 × 0.46 cm)
a 1.09 × 0.79 cm well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow
a small left hydrocele
serum CA19-9 level of 57.5 U/mL (normal <27 U/mL)
alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and other tumor markers were within normal limits

The patient has bilateral epididymal cysts, which is consistent with epididymal cysts.
The patient has a small left hydrocele, which is consistent with a hydrocele.
The patient presents with acute worsening of testicular pain, which could be suggestive of testicular torsion.
The patient has epididymal cysts, which could be associated with epididymitis.
The patient presents with a left testicular mass, which could be suggestive of a varicocele.
The patient presents with a testicular mass and elevated CA19-9 level, which could be suggestive of spermatocytic seminoma.

rationales.F01: Chronic testicular symptoms may be associated with testicular cancer.
rationales.F02: Acute worsening of symptoms could indicate testicular torsion or epididymitis.
rationales.F04: Enlarged and firm testis is concerning for testicular cancer.
rationales.F05: Negative transillumination suggests a solid mass, which could be testicular cancer.
rationales.F06: Bilateral epididymal cysts are common and not specific to any diagnosis.
rationales.F07: A well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion with internal blood flow is highly suggestive of testicular cancer.
rationales.F08: A small hydrocele can be associated with testicular cancer or other conditions.
rationales.F09: Elevated CA19-9 level is concerning for testicular cancer, although not specific.
rationales.F10: Normal tumor markers do not rule out testicular cancer, as some types may not produce elevated markers.
